::: {#exm-flat-prior-posterior}
#### Posterior mode and maximum likelihood estimate for a probability

In @exm-beta-bernoulli the prior is uniform on $(0, 1)$,
so by @cor-flat-prior-posterior the posterior density,
proportional to $\pi^{55}(1-\pi)^{36}$,
is maximized at the maximum likelihood estimate.
Setting the derivative of the log-likelihood $r \log \pi + (n - r)\log(1 - \pi)$,
which is $r/\pi - (n - r)/(1 - \pi)$,
to zero gives
$\hat\pi = r/n = 55/91 \approx `r round(55 / 91, 3)`$.
The posterior *mean*, $56/93 \approx `r round(56 / 93, 3)`$,
is not the maximum likelihood estimate:
@cor-flat-prior-posterior concerns the posterior's shape,
and so its mode, but a mean depends on the whole distribution.
:::
